ma_redemption_crag.blurb: A small, low cliff of about 35 feet in the Leominster area of central Massachusetts, used as a quieter fallback when the bigger ledge at Crow Hill is busy. The eleven routes are mostly traditional leads and top-rope laps, with the bulk of them at 5.7 and a few at 5.8 and 5.9, so it suits newer leaders and anyone building mileage. The gneiss is good quality and the face sits in sun for most of the day, which helps it dry quickly after rain, particularly once the leaves are off the trees. It makes an easy half-day outing rather than a destination.

ma_lower_skyport.blurb: Lower Skyport is a cluster of large, highly featured blocks in the Neverland zone of a state wildlife management area in western Massachusetts. It is the last stop in the zone, only a couple of minutes' walk from the parking lot and tucked behind another boulder group. Eleven bouldering problems range from V1 up to V7, centred on the V3 to V5 range, so there is something for solid intermediate climbers as well as a few harder lines. Several of the problems here are considered classics of the wider Skyport area, and the mantel tops are said to dry faster if you clear the dirt off them.

ma_swamp_2_boulders.blurb: A small bouldering spot on Cape Ann, part of the Great Swamp section of a large reservation of boulders on the Massachusetts North Shore. Three or four blocks sit roughly midway around the swamp and can be seen from the boardwalk. One block stands around 13 feet, while a taller one near 25 feet lies a short distance downhill toward the water. The eleven problems run from V1 to V7, with a fairly even spread through the middle grades and a handful of tougher lines, including a direct variation of the area's best-known problem. Good for a short session combined with the neighbouring swamp boulders.
